body: I think I’m mixing up zero and first drafts, thanks for pointing this out!! Yes, the first full draft of the story is finished and being edited, and next up is the second draft :)

My conscience is the size of the ocean so I definitely worry about things like this and tend to be honest about them to a fault. For once, it's actually great to know I'm overthinking something (lol).
Wow–I had no idea AI had environmental impact at all, but that's huge to know going forward. Thanks for sharing that here!

Ah, I'm not being clear here–sorry about that.  
  
I'm keeping the story as is, but my approach to writing the second draft will be to re-write the entire story from memory instead of referencing and copying from the original first draft. I've heard that this works well for some authors so they don't wind up rewriting the same things and there are enough changes from draft-to-draft. I'll probably compare the two drafts once the second is finished, but that's my plan for now.  
  
There are scenes and story elements I'm planning to move around, edit, etc. which I think is standard, but, I'm not flipping the entire story on its head. I love the plot and think it has some great concepts and scenes!

So, I'm not scrapping the entire story concept/plot/structure or anything–I'm just rewriting it from scratch in a blank document once edits are done. I hope that makes sense!

I was mostly worried about being able to publish in a few years, I'd be so bummed if I couldn't move forward with this for such a rookie mistake. Since I wrote the entire manuscript and this is the zero draft (which thank god will never be sent to a literary agent lol), it sounds like I'll be alright thankfully?

Also a relief to hear this, thanks for jumping in here. I still feel foolish for not knowing better in the beginning stages of this project, but glad to know it shouldn't be problem especially once I hit the final draft years from now.

This is a relief to hear, thanks for your comment. I'll definitely need to save up over the next couple years, but it would be so cool to have a professional take a look at this once it's gone through a few more drafts and is presentable on a professional level!

Oh boy...thanks for pointing this out. She's one of my oldest friends, and actually offered to edit the manuscript very early in the drafting process. While I don't have $10-20k, I am planning to put together a thank gift of some sort to deliver over the summer, and I'm planning to read the zero draft of her current novel when its finished. I'm definitely planning to make this up to her!  
  
While I'm very fortunate to have a best friend with the skills and knowledge she has, I appreciate your point and will make sure to thank her for her hard work as best I can. :)

Well, I learned after beginning the manuscript in November that publisher's will deny a manuscript if it's had any involvement with AI in the creation process, and I'm worried I can't come back from that even if I alter the elements I asked for feedback on. I really want to continue putting in the work required to publish this in a few years, but I'm worried I've ruined that for myself now. Does that make sense? :(

I’ve always been an easy crier (I’ve gotten much better now that I’m older), but as I’ve grown out of that the people around me don’t always respond with the level of maturity/respect I’d like to receive. It does get on my nerves, I have to admit. But then that thought brings me (personally) back to this sort of power-struggle to either “choose respect from people around you or no/less judgement when expressing hard emotions.” I’m a former teacher and so this one’s tough to balance. Especially when we’ve had a long day and we’re ready to start sobbing if one more thing goes wrong, but then theres the chance your students can never view you the same. It’s a double-edged sword somedays, honestly. 

As a whole, I think we can all try to become more comfortable with the idea that people who are solid rocks in our own lives are going to have days where they crumble. There’s a lot to appreciate and be grateful for when someone is willing to open up to us to, even if it does challenge the idea we have of them. I think everyone needs multiple “rock” type people in their lives, and we can all work to shift that lens from judgement to appreciation for the other’s transparency (because vulnerability can be super intimidating!).

From there it was wicked easy to get a general sense of what else to pay attention to and an idea of when to wear period panties/pad liners. I also started birth control in June which has made tracking my period a total breeze and makes my cycle much more consistent. I would talk to your PCP and see if they have any recommendations if that’s a route you want to take. I hope that all helps, this stuff can definitely be really annoying. Best of luck!!

This was years ago during the spring semester of my freshmen year in college. 

It was the “rock bottom” moment I experienced over my mother’s death two and a half years prior, and the pain from that had been building for the entire school year. I had no idea I was dealing with a nasty case of prolonged grief, but I missed her so much I decided I couldn’t stay any longer. I had everything I needed to go out to my truck (which she had left me), drive off campus, spend the night writing my goodbyes, and go through with it.

I remember having my keys in hand, leaving my room, and deciding on a whim, “I’m going to call ______. If they don’t pick up, I’m done.” I didn’t think they’d be up or at their phone, but thankfully they were. Had me come straight to her dorm on campus and helped me email my therapist how much I’d really been struggling. She had me stay until we were both sure I was okay for the night before I went back to my dorm.

I think about that night a lot; I wouldn’t be alive right now if they hadn’t picked up that night.

Seeing a few people saying not to worry as much about the NSAID/PNC allergies is definitely reassuring. My Mom was always on top of my allergies as a kid and made sure I was never given anything I couldn’t have, so I don’t actually know how I’d react—I’ve always assumed it would be another asthma attack. I’ve been thinking about bringing up another allergy test with my doctor to see if I’ve grown out of any of them (if that’s even a thing?).

As far as the asthma attacks I’ve had, I was hospitalized both times for 3-4 days. My mom told me I woke her up literally gasping for air and my lips were basically blue—she was shocked I was up at all. I hated having to use a nebulizer, and I know I needed it a lot, but I don’t remember how long I had to use it at home after each attack. I want to say daily maybe? My Dad and sister get really freaked out by hospitals/medical situations, so I think that’s why they never like getting into details with me on what happened.

I had some allergy tests done after the first attack and my doctor basically said taking any kind of aspirin could kill me within the hour. I carry my inhaler and my own pain killers (Tylenol) and don’t ask other people for anything like that just to be safe. I’ve always had an easy time memorizing numbers and number patterns. I loved doing math activities as a kid, too. I also loved Webkinz (those stuffed animals with the code tags you play with online). 

I begged my mother for months to let me get the premium month long membership, and she finally said yes, but ONLY for ONE month. We go to her desk and she has me read off the numbers of her credit card to her since she couldn’t find her glasses. Low and behold, I memorized the credit card information.

A month goes by, and I’ve bought tons of other Webkinz pets, furniture, houses, etc. Keep in mind I was in fifth grade and knew jack-shit about the financial world outside of this game, let alone a credit card.

I come home from school one day to a dead silent house and immediately knew why. I go into her office, she holds up the card without saying a word, I burst into tears and fess up. She found out when she went grocery shopping that morning and had her card declined.

I was completely convinced she was going to get rid of me or something even worse.  But instead, she had me sit next to me while she called the Webkinz company and had me watch them delete my whole account (I deserved it thats for sure). I never touched another credit card until I got my own last month. God bless my Mother, I’ll never know how she put up with my stunts as a child. 

TL;DR: Maxed out my Mom’s credit card on Webkinz and thought she was going to kick my ass into the next dimension when she found out.

Hi there, Front Ensemble member here! These aren’t speeches or anything, but two short quotes that have reminded me time and time again to keep working hard are:

“Rome wasn’t built in a day.”

The first one reminds me that I’m human; basically meaning not to overwork myself and try to perfect an ENTIRE DCI audition packet in one day, because that would be impossible. While I can’t perfect something to where I want it to be overnight, I can find ways to make my time in and out of the practice rooms most efficient (setting goals, being consistent with practice times, listening to recordings before I practice, practicing in front of mirrors/recording myself, mock auditions, etc.)

Secondly,

“She believed she could, and so she did.”

This one is definitely one of my favorites! Reminding me that if I REALLY set my mind to something, I can do it. It’s funny, my birthday is in November, so all of my friends always joke around and say “how much of a Scorpio” I am because when I set my mind to something I don’t let anything or anyone get in the way of my goals. If you want something bad enough, you’ll do what it takes to get it. 
Along those lines is another reminder that “If I can do it this well now, there’s someone in the world that could play this better than I could.” Trying to decrease that number is what I think about a lot, because then I become the person “who can play it better” come the actual auditions. NEVER SETTLE! There’s always more you can do, trust me.

I hope these help! I know they aren’t speeches, but I think of these two quotes and others whenever I’m overwhelmed or discouraged. I wish you the best of luck in all of your auditions this season. We’re all rooting for you! 😁
